answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: each transition damps a seed’s probability mass, while a sybil cluster’s sparse boundary limits escape. For S, low conductance φ(S)=w(∂S)/vol(S), together with mixing and min-cut transitivity bounds, caps its stationary mass and aggregate voting weight absent trusted inflow. Thus a summit cannot make sybils wander freely; even a karst-like cluster remains isolated.
